Update in relation to the publication of Annual Report and Accounts
MobilityOne (AIM: MBO), the e-commerce infrastructure payment solutions and platform provider, provides the following update in relation to its annual report and accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 ("
FY 2025
").
On 30 June 2026 the Company announced, amongst other matters, that the preparation of the Company's financial statements for FY 2025 has been ongoing and that the Company expects the audited FY 2025 accounts to be published by the end of July 2026. While the Company has made substantial progress in relation to the preparation of its financial statements for FY 2025 and is nearing completion of the audit process, the finalisation of the audited accounts remains ongoing.
Accordingly, the Company now expects the audited FY 2025 accounts to be published in August 2026.
The Company's ordinary shares remain suspended pending publication of the audited FY 2025 accounts.

About the Group:
MobilityOne
is one of the leading virtual distributors of mobile prepaid reload and bill payment services in Malaysia. With connections to various service providers across industries such as banking, telecommunications, utilities, government agencies, and transportation, the Group operates through multiple distribution channels including mobile wallets, e-commerce sites, EDC terminals, automated teller machines, kiosks, and internet & mobile banking. Holding licenses in regulated spaces including acquiring, e-money, remittance and lending, the Group offers a range of services to the market, including wallet, internet, and terminal-based payment services, white label e-money, remittance, lending, and custom fintech ecosystems for communities. The Group's flexible, scalable technology platform enables cash, debit card, and credit card transactions from multiple devices while providing robust control and monitoring of product and service distribution.

Delay in publication of Annual Report and Accounts
Temporary suspension from trading on AIM
MobilityOne (AIM: MBO), the e-commerce infrastructure payment solutions and platform provider, announces that its audited annual report and accounts for the year ended 31 December 2025 ("
FY 2025
") will not be finalised by the end of June 2026, as stipulated under Rule 19 of the AIM Rules for Companies.
The preparation of the Company's financial statements for FY 2025 has been ongoing. Notwithstanding this, despite the best efforts of all parties, the auditors in the UK have requested additional analysis to be completed by the Company's component auditors in Malaysia. This additional analysis is in connection with the Group's 49% owned associate company, Sincere Acres Sdn Bhd and its wholly owned subsidiary, Hati International Sdn Bhd ("
Hati
"). In particular, in relation to the impact of the winding up petition that Hati was subject to in December 2025, as announced by the Company on 22 December 2025, and the carrying value of the associate company in the Group accounts. A stay of execution of the winding up order was granted pending the outcome of an appeal, which is expected by the end of 2026.
Accordingly, the Company expects the accounts to be published in July 2026.
This delay to the publication of the audited FY 2025 annual accounts means that trading in the Company's ordinary shares on AIM will be suspended with effect from 7:30 a.m. on 1 July 2026 and will remain suspended until the publication of its audited FY 2025 annual accounts.
The Company will release further announcements as and when appropriate.

The Second Tranche Payment Date has been subject to several prior extensions, as announced by the Company most recently on 16 March 2026.

In line with the Second Tranche payment terms, any payment made in relation to the outstanding amounts on the Second Tranche will continue to be subject to an interest charge of 10% per annum.

MobilityOne (AIM: MBO), the e-commerce infrastructure payment solutions and platform provider, notes the recent media commentary stating,
inter alia
, that MobilityOne Sdn Bhd has secured a full-fledged Shariah-compliant Islamic digital banking licence from the Labuan Financial Services Authority.
On 31 December 2025, MobilityOne announced that MobilityOne Sdn Bhd ("
M1
Malaysia
"), the Group's wholly-owned operating subsidiary in Malaysia, had received conditional approval from Labuan Financial Services Authority ("
Labuan
FSA
") for M1 Malaysia to establish a subsidiary in Labuan to be named MBO Bank (Labuan) Limited ("
MBO
Bank
"), to carry on Islamic digital banking business in Labuan, Malaysia.
As further outlined in the announcement, the conditional approval is subject to,
inter alia

company_30s.what_they_do: MBO.L is a small, largely unproven technology firm that claims to be developing mobile‑money transfer solutions for emerging markets.  Its public filings suggest it is still in the early stages of building its product and has yet to generate significant revenue.
company_30s.why_they_matter: If it succeeds, it would tap into a growing demand for digital payment platforms in developing economies, a segment that is attracting a lot of investor attention.  The company’s potential lies in its ability to partner with local telecoms and banks to offer low‑cost, mobile‑first financial services.
company_30s.current_state: The company appears to be in a cash‑burn phase, juggling regulatory hurdles and funding extensions.  Recent filings show a pause on the SEC registration deadline, hinting at a possible liquidation if the extension is denied.  The share price is negligible, trading at pennies, and the market has largely moved on.

rns_narrative: The latest RNS items focus on administrative updates—annual reports, a suspension notice, and a joint‑venture proposal that never materialised.  No new product launches or revenue milestones appear.
The company’s narrative is one of survival: it is attempting to extend its regulatory filing window while seeking additional capital, but the filings do not indicate any substantive progress.
There is no evidence of a turnaround; instead, the company is stuck in a regulatory limbo that could lead to delisting.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silent caution – the community is largely indifferent, with a handful of skeptical comments about funding and regulatory compliance.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: There are no active bull voices; the only bullish chatter is a generic hope that the company will secure new investors and clear its SEC registration.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the failed joint venture, the pending SEC extension, and the lack of any revenue as red flags.  They argue the company is likely to be liquidated if it cannot meet its filing deadline.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The sentiment has stayed flat over the past month.  A few neutral posts about backers and extensions keep the conversation alive, but there is no real momentum building in either direction.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for MBO.L are dead—no recent spikes in search volume.  This lack of public interest means a surprise catalyst could still generate a sharp price move if it materialises.

near_term_catalysts: SEC registration deadline: if the company secures a 30‑day extension or clears the filing, it could keep the stock alive.
Funding announcement: a new round of capital or a partnership with a telecom operator would signal a shift from survival to growth.
Regulatory clearance: any positive update from the SEC or a local regulator would remove the immediate delisting risk.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume accompanied by a news release about funding or regulatory approval.  A jump in volume above the 50‑day average would be the clearest confirmation that the market is moving.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is in a very early stage of its crash‑recovery cycle—essentially a pre‑crash or flat phase.  Without a clear catalyst, the mean‑reversion thesis is weak.  Only a decisive regulatory or funding event could push the price back up.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company were to secure a major funding round or clear its SEC filing, the price could rebound from its current penny level to a few pence—an 800‑to‑1 upside.  However, this scenario is highly speculative and hinges on a single, uncertain event.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company is on the brink of delisting if it fails to meet its regulatory deadline.  Even a brief pause in trading could trigger a liquidation event.  The absence of revenue, coupled with a history of missed milestones, suggests a realistic downside of 100% if the company is wound down.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is enormous, but the probability is tiny.  The risk is a total wipe‑out of the investment if the company is liquidated.  The asymmetry is therefore highly negative for a contrarian trader.

playbook.if_bullish: Not recommended.  The only entry point would be a sudden, credible funding announcement, which is unlikely.  If you still want to test, buy a single share at the current price with a stop‑loss at the next support level (a few pence).  Position size should be negligible.
playbook.if_watching: Monitor the SEC filing deadline and any news about new investors.  Trigger a buy if there is a confirmed extension or a funding announcement that includes a clear use‑of‑proceeds plan.
playbook.if_passing: If the company fails to secure the SEC extension or if a delisting notice is issued, exit immediately.  The terminal risk of liquidation makes this a pass‑or‑die situation.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MBO.L is a highly speculative, near‑liquidation risk with no clear catalysts—unless a major funding or regulatory event suddenly appears, the stock is unlikely to recover from its current depth.
